The First Amendment free speech clause (applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment) protects the free flow of ideas with limited exceptions. A law that infringes upon this right can be challenged on its face and struck down in its entirety under either:

  • the overbreadth doctrine – renders laws unconstitutional if they restrict a substantial amount of protected speech or
  • the vagueness doctrine – renders laws unconstitutional if ordinary persons would have to guess the law's meaning because the law fails to provide notice of what speech is prohibited.

Here, the state statute regulates speech by prohibiting retailers from publicly displaying or selling any material containing violent or sexually explicit pictures that may be harmful to minors. Although some violent or sexually explicit speech is not protected by the First Amendment, a substantial amount is. Therefore, the overbreadth doctrine is a defense against the enforcement of this statute. And since this statute also requires ordinary persons to guess as to which materials may be harmful to minors, the vagueness doctrine is another valid defense.

(Choices A & B) The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause prohibits states from treating similarly situated persons (or classes of persons) differently without adequate justification. But here, there is no evidence that this law is being applied in a discriminatory manner—eg, had corner store owners, but no other retailers, been prosecuted under the statute. Therefore, an equal protection defense would likely fail.

(Choice C) A state may prohibit the sale of violent or sexually explicit material if (1) it falls outside of the First Amendment's protections—eg, material that incites crime or is obscene under the Miller test—or (2) this content-based restriction passes strict scrutiny. Neither requires proof that the material is utterly without any redeeming value in the marketplace of ideas.

📌 Educational Objective

A law that interferes with the freedom of speech will be struck down on its face if it restricts a substantial amount of protected speech (ie, overbroad) OR fails to give ordinary persons notice of the prohibited speech (ie, unduly vague).

📚 References
  • Watchtower Bible & Tract Soc'y of N.Y., Inc. v. Vill. of Stratton, 536 U.S. 150, 165 (2002) (finding an ordinance overbroad since it prohibits all door-to-door, not just commercial, canvassing without a license).
  • Gentile v. State Bar of Nev., 501 U.S. 1030, 1057–58 (1991) (striking down a law for vagueness since it tends to mislead attorneys about potential punishment for pretrial publicity of clients' criminal defenses).
questions.zh-question:
某州法规禁止任何书籍、杂志、图片或海报的零售商“向任何人公开展示或销售任何因其图像内容的暴力或色情性质而可能对未成年人有害的材料”。违反本法规属轻罪。

一家街角商店公开展示并销售含有暴力和色情图片的杂志。该店主因这些行为根据上述法规被起诉。

在州初审法院为此案进行辩护时，以下哪项是该街角商店的最佳辩护理由？

zh-choices.A: 法律的平等保护，因为该法规不合理地区分了可能损害未成年人的暴力和色情图像材料，以及仅可能损害成年人的此类材料。
zh-choices.B: 法律的平等保护，因为该法规不合理地将图像形式的暴力和色情材料与完全由印刷文字组成的此类材料区别对待。
zh-choices.C: 经由第十四修正案合并适用于各州的宪法第一修正案，因为在没有证据证明材料在思想市场上完全没有任何可取价值的情况下，一个州不得禁止销售暴力或色情材料。
zh-choices.D: 经由第十四修正案合并适用于各州的宪法第一修正案，因为该法规过度模糊和过分宽泛。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: First Amendment
最佳辩护理由 (Best Defense) 选项 D： 经由第十四修正案合并适用于各州的宪法第一修正案，因为该法规过度模糊和过分宽泛 (Vague and Overbroad)。

本题考查的是对言论自由限制的表面违宪审查 (Facial Challenge)。当法规涉及言论自由时，如果其措辞不当，即使被告的行为本身可能不受保护，被告仍可主张该法规整体违宪。

1. 过度宽泛 (Overbreadth)

定义：如果一项法律在禁止不受保护的言论（如淫秽内容）的同时，也禁止了大量的受保护言论，则该法律是“过度宽泛”的。

本案分析：

  • 法规禁止向任何人 (any person) 销售可能对未成年人有害的材料。
  • 这意味着成年人也无法购买这些材料。
  • 关键判例：在 Butler v. Michigan (1957) 中，最高法院指出，州政府不能为了保护未成年人，而将成年人的阅读范围限制在适合儿童的水平（"burn the house to roast the pig"）。
  • 因此，该法规侵犯了成年人获取受第一修正案保护的非淫秽材料的权利。
2. 模糊性 (Vagueness)

定义：根据正当程序条款 (Due Process Clause)，如果法律未能给普通人提供关于何种行为被禁止的合理通知 (Reasonable Notice)，则该法律无效。

本案分析：

  • 法规使用了“可能对未成年人有害 (may be harmful to minors)”这一表述。
  • 如果没有具体的定义或标准（如具体的年龄分级或明确的淫秽定义），店主必须去猜测什么内容是违法的。
  • 这种不确定性会产生寒蝉效应 (Chilling Effect)，导致人们为了避免受罚而不敢行使合法的言论自由权利。
为什么其他选项是错的？
🚫 选项 A & B (Equal Protection)：

虽然平等保护条款禁止不合理的分类，但在言论自由案件中，如果法律直接限制了言论内容，法院首选的分析工具是第一修正案，而不是平等保护。此外，区分“文字与图片”或“成人与儿童的伤害”通常能通过合理性审查 (Rational Basis)，但这并不能解决其侵犯言论自由的核心问题。

🚫 选项 C (Redeeming Value)：

这个选项引用了一个过时的标准。现在的淫秽定义来自 Miller v. California，要求材料缺乏“严肃的文学、艺术、政治或科学价值”。法律不需要证明材料“完全没有任何 (utterly without any)”价值就能禁止它。只要符合 Miller 标准，州政府就可以监管。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧：

当你看到题目中的法规原文包含广泛的禁止性语言（如 "any material", "any person"）且涉及言论内容时，首先要考虑Overbreadth（过度宽泛）和Vagueness（模糊性）。

如果法规为了保护儿童而限制了成年人的访问权，这几乎总是违反第一修正案的。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A doctor who was licensed to practice medicine in a particular state was convicted in state court of improperly distributing specified drugs by writing prescriptions for fictitious persons. Under state law, such an abuse of the prescription-writing privilege requires revocation of a doctor's license. After it received an official notification of the doctor's conviction, the state medical board revoked the doctor's license without affording him any opportunity for a hearing.
The doctor has sued the board in state court to set aside the revocation, alleging deprivation of property without due process of law because the board did not provide an opportunity for a trial-type hearing before revoking the license. The doctor does not deny the conviction or the factual basis for it.
Which of the following is the strongest argument in support of the state medical board?

choices.A: A doctor's license to practice is a privilege, not a right, and therefore is not property within the meaning of the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.B: Due process requires a balancing of interests, and the state's interest in preventing drug abuse outweighs the doctor's interest in the particular procedure followed in the disciplinary proceeding.
choices.C: The adjudicative facts necessary to revoke the doctor's license were determined in the criminal trial, and therefore due process does not require any further trial-type hearing.
choices.D: The licensing board was required to summarily revoke the doctor's license because Article IV, Section 1, of the Constitution requires the licensing board to give full faith and credit to the doctor's criminal conviction.

questions.explanation:
Procedural due process
(Mathews v. Eldridge balancing test)
Private interest
affected by
deprivation
Risk of erroneous
deprivation + Value
of other safeguards
Government interest
(administrative &
fiscal burdens)
Insufficient process
Sufficient process

Procedural due process requires that the government provide reasonable notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard before a neutral decision-maker when depriving persons of life, liberty, or property. To determine whether the government provided due process, courts balance three factors:

  • the private interest affected by the deprivation
  • the risk of erroneous deprivation of that interest through current procedures and the probable value of additional or substitute procedural safeguards and
  • the government's interest, including the fiscal and administrative burdens that other safeguards would entail.

Here, the doctor's property interest in his medical license is likely outweighed by the state's interest in preventing drug abuse—particularly since additional or substitute proceedings would fiscally and administratively burden the medical board. And the risk of erroneously depriving the doctor of his license is low given the protections afforded in his related criminal proceeding. Therefore, the board's strongest argument is that the facts necessary to revoke the doctor's license were determined in the criminal trial, so no further trial-type hearing is required.

(Choice A) Due process protections historically extended to rights—not privileges. But this distinction has been abandoned, and such protections extend to any legitimate life, liberty, or property interest.

(Choice B) Due process does require a balancing of interests. But it weighs the state's interest in preventing drug abuse against the doctor's interest in his license (not the board's particular procedures) and the risks of current procedures and value of alternative safeguards.

(Choice D) Under the full faith and credit clause, a valid judgment issued in one state must be recognized in every other state. This clause does not apply here since the doctor's conviction and license revocation occurred in the same state. But even if it did, the state need only honor the criminal conviction—not revoke the doctor's license.

📌 Educational Objective

Procedural due process is assessed by weighing three factors: (1) the private interest affected, (2) the risk of erroneous deprivation of that interest and probable value of other procedural safeguards, and (3) the government's interest, including the fiscal and administrative burdens that other safeguards would entail.

📚 References
  • Mathews v. Eldridge, 424 U.S. 319, 335 (1976) (listing the three factors used to assess compliance with procedural due process).
questions.zh-question:
一名在某州获得行医执照的医生，因给虚构人物开具处方，不当分发特定药物而被州法院定罪。根据州法律，滥用处方权的此种行为需要吊销医生的执照。州医疗委员会在收到该医生被定罪的正式通知后，未经听证程序即吊销了该医生的执照。

该医生已向州法院起诉该委员会，要求撤销吊销决定，声称委员会在吊销其执照前未提供审判式听证的机会，侵犯了其未经正当法律程序而被剥夺财产的权利。该医生并未否认其定罪或其事实依据。

以下哪项是支持州医疗委员会的最有力论点？

zh-choices.A: 医生的行医执照是一种特权，而非权利，因此不属于《第十四修正案》正当程序条款所指的财产。
zh-choices.B: 正当程序要求利益衡量，而州在防止药物滥用方面的利益，重于医生在纪律处分程序中所遵循的特定程序中的利益。
zh-choices.C: 吊销医生执照所需的裁决性事实已在刑事审判中确定，因此正当程序不要求任何进一步的审判式听证。
zh-choices.D: 执照委员会被要求立即吊销医生的执照，因为《宪法》第四条第一款要求执照委员会对医生的刑事定罪给予充分信任和尊重。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Procedural Due Process
⚖️ 核心考点：Mathews v. Eldridge 测试

在决定政府剥夺个人财产（如执照）前需要何种程序时，法院使用三要素平衡测试：

  1. 私人利益 (Private Interest)：被剥夺权益的重要性。
  2. 错误风险 (Risk of Error)：现有程序的出错概率及额外程序的价值。
  3. 政府利益 (Government Interest)：行政效率和财政负担。

✅ 为什么选 C？

正确答案 裁决性事实已在刑事审判中确定

本题的关键在于 Mathews 测试的第二个要素：额外程序的价值。

医生已经被刑事法庭定罪。刑事审判的证明标准是“排除合理怀疑” (Beyond a reasonable doubt)，这是最高的证明标准。既然事实已经在刑事法庭上被严格证实，那么在行政听证会上再次确认这些事实（通常仅需“优势证据”标准）是毫无必要的重复。

因此，在此情境下，举行听证会来确认“医生是否开了假处方”这一事实，其错误剥夺的风险几乎为零，额外听证会的价值也为零。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

高频陷阱 选项 B：利益衡量 (Balancing of Interests)

这是一个精心设计的干扰项。虽然正当程序确实涉及“利益衡量”，但选项 B 的表述是错误的。

它错误地将“政府防止药物滥用的宏观利益”与“医生对特定程序的微观利益”进行对比。真正的 Mathews 测试衡量的是：增加额外程序的行政负担 vs. 该程序减少错误判决的价值。选项 B 忽略了本案中“事实已被刑事定罪确认”这一核心逻辑。

错误观念 选项 A：权利 vs. 特权 (Right vs. Privilege)

这是一个过时的法律概念。现代宪法学（自 Goldberg v. Kelly 等案以来）已经废弃了“权利与特权”的区别。职业执照被视为受第十四修正案保护的财产利益 (Property Interest)。

适用错误 选项 D：充分信任和尊重 (Full Faith and Credit)

该条款 (Article IV, Section 1) 主要适用于州与州之间承认判决。本案是同一个州内部的刑事法院和行政机构之间的关系，因此该条款不适用。

💡 MBE 解题技巧：
当题目涉及“基于刑事定罪的行政处罚”时，通常不需要新的事实听证会。因为刑事定罪提供了最高级别的程序保护，这本身就满足了 Due Process 对事实认定的要求。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A purchaser bought land in the mountain foothills just outside a resort town and planned to build a housing development there. Soon thereafter, the county in which the land was located unexpectedly adopted a regulation that, for the first time, prohibited all construction in several foothill and mountain areas, including the area of the purchaser's property. The purpose of the county's regulation was "to conserve for future generations the unique natural wildlife and plant habitats" in the mountain areas. Since the adoption of the regulation, the purchaser has been unable to lease or sell the property at any price. Several realtors have advised the purchaser that his property is now worthless.
The purchaser has sued the county, claiming that the regulation has effected a taking of the purchaser's property and that the county therefore owes the purchaser just compensation.
Is the court likely to rule in favor of the purchaser?

choices.A: No, because the county did not take title to the property from the purchaser.
choices.B: No, because the regulation has not caused or authorized any uninvited physical invasion or intrusion onto the property.
choices.C: Yes, because the conservation objective of the county ordinance is not sufficiently compelling to justify the substantial diminution in the property value.
choices.D: Yes, because the effect of the county's regulation is to deny the purchaser's investment-backed expectation and essentially all economically beneficial use of the property.

questions.explanation:
Fifth Amendment takings
Type Attributes
Physical • Possession or permanent physical invasion of property
Regulatory • Deprivation of all economically beneficial uses
• Restricts use under totality of circumstances:
◦ character of government action
◦ economic impact
◦ reasonable investment-back expectations
Exaction • Condition to obtain building/development permit
Destruction • Destruction of property or property interest (eg, easements, liens)

A taking occurs when the government:

  • physically possesses or invades private property (ie, physical taking) or
  • deprives the owner of all economically beneficial use of the property but the owner retains possession (ie, regulatory taking) (Choices A & B).

And under the Fifth Amendment—as applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment—a taking must be for a public use, and the government must justly compensate the owner for the property's fair market value.

Here, the county's regulation prohibits all construction on the purchaser's land. This amounted to a regulatory taking because it denied the purchaser (1) his investment-backed expectation for the planned housing development and (2) essentially all economically beneficial use of the property. And since the property was rendered worthless, the court will likely rule that the purchaser is entitled to just compensation.

(Choice C) The ordinance's objective to conserve natural wildlife and plant habitats may be compelling. But the county can only justify the substantial diminution in the purchaser's property value by providing him just compensation.

📌 Educational Objective

A Fifth Amendment taking occurs when (1) the government physically possesses or invades private property or (2) the owner retains possession but loses all economically beneficial use of the property due to government action.

📚 References
  • Lucas v. S.C. Coastal Council, 505 U.S. 1003, 1019 (1992) (holding that a deprivation of all economically beneficial uses of property constitutes a taking).
  • 26 Am Jur. 2d Eminent Domain § 12 (2019) (explaining a deprivation of all economically beneficial uses of property).
questions.zh-question:
一名购买者在一个度假小镇外的山麓地带购买了土地，并计划在那里建造一个住宅开发项目。此后不久，该土地所在的县出人意料地通过了一项法规，首次禁止在包括购买者财产所在区域在内的几个山麓和山区进行所有建设。该县法规的目的是“为后代保护山区独特的自然野生动植物栖息地”。自该法规通过以来，购买者一直无法以任何价格出租或出售该房产。几位房地产经纪人已告知购买者，他的财产现在一文不值。

购买者已起诉该县，声称该法规构成了对其财产的征收，因此该县应向购买者支付公正补偿。

法院是否可能作出有利于购买者的裁决？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该县并未从购买者手中取得该财产的所有权。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该法规并未导致或授权任何未经邀请的对该财产的物理侵占或侵入。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该县法令的保护目标不足以成为财产价值大幅减损的正当理由。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该县法规的效果是剥夺了购买者有投资支持的预期，以及该财产基本上所有的经济上有利的用途。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：管制性征收
Regulatory Takings

本题考察的是美国宪法第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）中的征收条款（Takings Clause），特别是当政府法规导致财产价值完全丧失时的法律后果。

正确答案：D

深度解析

法院很可能会判决购买者胜诉，理由如下：

1. 管制性征收 (Regulatory Taking)
虽然政府没有物理上占有土地，但如果一项法规剥夺了所有者对该财产“所有经济上有利的用途” (all economically beneficial use)，这在法律上被视为一种“本身即构成征收” (per se taking)。

2. 事实认定
题目中明确指出：

  • 法规禁止了所有建设 (prohibited all construction)。
  • 该财产现在一文不值 (worthless)。
  • 购买者无法出售或租赁该土地。
这种程度的限制完全剥夺了购买者“有投资支持的预期” (investment-backed expectations)，即开发房产的计划。

3. 结论
根据第五修正案，当法规效果等同于完全剥夺财产价值时，政府必须支付公正补偿 (Just Compensation)，无论政府的初衷（如环境保护）多么高尚。

关键判例 (Key Precedent)

Lucas v. South Carolina Coastal Council (1992)

最高法院在该案中确立了规则：当一项法规剥夺了土地所有者100%的经济价值时，除非该限制源于普通法中的妨害（nuisance）原则，否则政府必须进行赔偿。这就是著名的“卢卡斯规则” (Lucas Rule)。

为什么其他选项是错的？

  • 选项 A 错误：征收不需要政府获得所有权 (title)。只要政府行为剥夺了财产的使用权或价值，即可构成征收。
  • 选项 B 错误：这混淆了物理性征收 (Physical Taking) 和管制性征收。虽然没有物理入侵，但法规限制本身已构成征收。
  • 选项 C 错误：这是一个常见的陷阱。虽然保护环境是合法的警察权 (Police Power) 行使，但这并不能免除政府在造成“完全经济价值丧失”时的赔偿责任。目的正当不代表可以免费剥夺私产。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The Federal Family Film Enhancement Act assesses an excise tax of 10% on the price of admission to public movie theaters when they show films that contain actual or simulated scenes of human sexual intercourse.
Which of the following is the strongest argument against the constitutionality of this federal act?

choices.A: The act imposes a prior restraint on the freedom of speech protected by the First Amendment.
choices.B: The act imposes a tax solely on the basis of the content of speech without adequate justification and, therefore, it is prohibited by the freedom of speech clause of the First Amendment.
choices.C: The act is not rationally related to any legitimate national interest.
choices.D: The act violates the equal protection concepts embodied in the due process clause of the Fifth Amendment because it imposes a tax on the price of admission to view certain films and not on the price of admission to view comparable live performances.

questions.explanation:
Speech regulations
Type Definition Test
Content-based
  • Facial discrimination
  • Primary purpose targets message, subject, or idea
Strict scrutiny
  • Necessary & narrowly tailored to achieve compelling interest
Content-neutral
  • Regulates time, place, or manner of speech
Intermediate scrutiny
  • Narrowly tailored to achieve important interest
  • Alternative avenues of communication remain

The First Amendment free speech clause protects the right to freely communicate and receive information and ideas. To ensure such protection, content-based restrictions on speech are presumptively unconstitutional and subject to strict scrutiny. This means that the government can only restrict speech based on what is being said (ie, its message or ideas) if it can prove that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest—a nearly impossible task.

Here, the act is a content-based restriction on speech because it imposes an excise tax on the price of admission to theaters when they show films that depict human sexual intercourse. And since it is highly unlikely that this act can survive strict scrutiny, the strongest argument against its constitutionality is that it imposes a tax based solely on the content of speech without adequate justification.

(Choice A) A prior restraint on speech is a highly disfavored government action that prohibits speech before it even occurs (eg, injunction). But the act here is not a prior restraint on speech because it does not prevent the films from being shown—it merely imposes a tax.

(Choice B) The act imposes a tax solely on the basis of the content of speech without adequate justification and, therefore, it is prohibited by the freedom of speech clause of the First Amendment.

(Choice C) If the federal act is not rationally related to a legitimate national interest, it cannot pass rational basis scrutiny—let alone strict scrutiny. But this argument would likely fail since laws almost always survive rational basis review.

(Choice D) This act may trigger the equal protection concepts embodied in the Fifth Amendment, which apply when the government treats similarly situated people differently. But since the movie theater patrons who must pay this tax are not part of a protected class, this is not a strong argument for challenging the act's validity.

📌 Educational Objective

Content-based restrictions on speech are unconstitutional unless they survive strict scrutiny. This incredibly stringent standard requires the government to prove that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest.

📚 References
  • Ark. Writers' Project, Inc. v. Ragland, 481 U.S. 221, 231 (1987) (applying strict scrutiny to a tax scheme that exempts certain magazines based on content).
questions.zh-question: 下列哪项是反对该联邦法案合宪性的最有力论点？

zh-choices.A: 该法案对受《第一修正案》保护的言论自由施加了事先限制。
zh-choices.B: 该法案仅基于言论内容征税，且无充分正当理由，因此，该行为被《第一修正案》的言论自由条款所禁止。
zh-choices.C: 该法案与任何合法的国家利益均不存在理性关联。
zh-choices.D: 该法案违反了《第五修正案》正当程序条款所体现的平等保护理念，因为它对观看某些电影的门票价格征税，而对观看可比的现场表演的门票价格则不征税。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法第一修正案与税收
核心原则：基于内容的规制 (Content-Based Regulation) 当政府对言论施加限制（包括税收）是基于言论的内容（即所表达的信息、主题或思想）时，该行为被推定为违宪，必须接受严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。
为何选项 B 是正确答案？

本题的核心在于识别该税收的性质。这项联邦税并非适用于所有电影票的通用销售税，而是专门针对包含特定内容（性交场景）的电影。

1. 识别歧视：
最高法院在 Arkansas Writers' Project, Inc. v. Ragland 等判例中确立，针对特定出版物或言论内容的差别税收（Differential Taxation）属于基于内容的规制。

2. 适用标准：
因为是基于内容的，政府必须证明该法律满足严格审查标准：

  • 必须为了实现迫切的政府利益 (Compelling Government Interest)。
  • 手段必须是狭义限定的 (Narrowly Tailored)。

3. 结论：
仅仅为了增加收入通常不足以构成“迫切利益”来正当化对言论内容的歧视。因此，最有力的论点是该法案基于内容征税且缺乏充分（迫切）的正当理由。

其他选项为何不够强？
选项 A 事先限制 (Prior Restraint)
虽然事先限制也是违宪的，但税收通常被视为事后的负担，而不是阻止言论发表的“禁令”或“许可制度”。除非税额高到构成事实上的禁止，否则法院更倾向于将其视为基于内容的惩罚，而非事先限制。
选项 C 理性基础 (Rational Basis)
这是一个陷阱。涉及言论自由的限制需要更高标准的审查（严格审查或中度审查），而不仅仅是“理性关联”。如果只用理性基础测试，政府很容易通过（例如声称为了保护家庭价值观），但这在第一修正案下是不够的。
选项 D 平等保护 (Equal Protection)
虽然差别待遇涉及平等保护，但在涉及基本权利（如言论自由）时，法院通常直接依据第一修正案进行分析。第一修正案的分析比第五修正案的平等保护分析更直接、更具体地针对言论内容歧视问题。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

看到政府对媒体、电影或出版物征税时，请立即检查：

  1. 通用税 (General Tax)：如果是对所有企业一视同仁的税，通常合宪。
  2. 特定税 (Specific Tax)：如果是专门针对媒体，或者针对特定内容的媒体征税，这就触发了严格审查。

本题中，“仅针对有性交场景的电影”就是明显的“基于内容”的信号。

Reference Case: Arkansas Writers' Project, Inc. v. Ragland, 481 U.S. 221 (1987).

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a statute that made it illegal for "any employee, without the consent of his or her employer, to post on the Internet any information concerning the employer." The purpose of the statute was to prevent employees from revealing their employers' trade secrets.
Is the statute constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it is not narrowly tailored to further a compelling government interest.
choices.B: No, because it targets a particular medium of communication for special regulation.
choices.C: Yes, because it leaves open ample alternative channels of communication.
choices.D: Yes, because it prevents employees from engaging in unethical conduct.

questions.explanation:
Free speech analysis
Content-based restriction
(message, subject, or idea)
Content-neutral restriction
(time, place, or manner)
Strict scrutiny
(least restrictive means)
  • Necessary & narrowly tailored to compelling interest
Intermediate scrutiny
(no greater than necessary)
  • Narrowly tailored to substantial interest
  • Alternative avenues of communication
Exception
(nonpublic forum + viewpoint-neutral)
Rational basis
Reasonably related to legitimate interest

The First Amendment free speech clause prohibits the government from unduly restricting an individual's right to freely communicate information and ideas. Restrictions based on the content of speech (ie, its message or ideas) are presumptively invalid and will only be upheld if they survive strict judicial scrutiny. Under this standard of review, the government has the nearly impossible task of proving that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored (ie, the least restrictive means) to further a compelling government interest.

Here, the statute targets speech based on its content since the statute prohibits employees from posting information concerning their employer. And though the government may have a compelling interest in preventing employees from revealing trade secrets, the statute is not necessary or narrowly tailored to further that interest. That is because less restrictive means could be used to protect trade secrets—eg, barring employees from posting information concerning their employers' trade secrets. As a result, the statute is unconstitutional.

(Choice B) A speech regulation does not violate the First Amendment simply because it targets a particular medium of communication (eg, Internet postings— as seen here).*

*In Packingham v. North Carolina, the Supreme Court equated the Internet to public streets and parks in dicta but never expressly held that the Internet is a public forum. Several cases dealing with this issue are currently being litigated in lower courts.

(Choice C) The availability of alternative channels of communication is one factor in evaluating content-neutral speech restrictions (ie, time, place, or manner restrictions). But since this statute is a content-based restriction, the fact that it leaves open other channels of communication other than the Internet is irrelevant.

(Choice D) The statute may prevent employees from engaging in unethical conduct (eg, revealing trade secrets). But regardless, it is unconstitutional because it cannot survive strict scrutiny.

📌 Educational Objective

Content-based restrictions on speech are presumptively invalid and will only be upheld if they survive strict scrutiny—ie, the government must prove that the restriction is necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest.

📚 References
  • United States v. Playboy Entm't Grp., 529 U.S. 803, 816–17 (2000) (explaining that content-based restrictions on speech require the government to satisfy strict scrutiny).
questions.zh-question:
国会颁布了一项法规，规定“任何雇员，未经其雇主同意，在互联网上发布任何有关其雇主的信息”均属非法。该法规的目的是防止雇员泄露其雇主的商业秘密。

该法规是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为它并非为促进某一重大的政府利益而经过严格限缩。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为它针对某一特定的传播媒介进行特别管制。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为它保留了充足的替代沟通渠道。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为它阻止了雇员从事不道德的行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Constitutional Law / First Amendment

核心考点：严格审查标准

基于内容的限制 (Content-Based Restriction)
如果政府对言论的限制是基于言论所传达的信息或主题，则该限制被推定为违宪。

对于此类限制，法院适用严格审查标准 (Strict Scrutiny)。政府必须证明该法律：

  1. 是为了实现重大的政府利益 (Compelling Government Interest)；且
  2. 手段是经过严格限缩的 / 必要的 (Narrowly Tailored / Necessary)。

本题逻辑链分析

1
定性：法规禁止发布“有关其雇主的信息”。要判断某条言论是否违规，执法者必须查看言论的内容。因此，这是基于内容的限制。
2
定标：既然是基于内容的限制，必须适用严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。
3
应用：
  • 目的：保护商业秘密 (Trade Secrets)。这可能是一个重大的政府利益。
  • 手段：禁止发布“任何”关于雇主的信息。
  • 结论：手段太宽泛了！它不仅禁止了商业秘密，还禁止了诸如“我老板今天穿了红衬衫”等无害言论。因此，它不是Narrowly Tailored。
✅ 正确答案 A
法律违宪，因为它没有经过严格限缩 (Not narrowly tailored) 以促进重大的政府利益。它打击面过广，限制了受第一修正案保护的无害言论。

为什么其他选项是错的？

❌ 选项 B (媒介管制)： 针对特定媒介（如互联网）的管制本身并不自动违宪。关键在于该管制是否基于内容。如果法律只是说“禁止在互联网上发垃圾邮件”（不看内容），标准会不同。
❌ 选项 C (替代渠道)： “充足的替代沟通渠道” (Ample alternative channels) 是内容中立 (Content-Neutral) 的“时间、地点、方式”限制 (Time, Place, and Manner Restrictions) 的审查要素。本题是基于内容的限制，不适用此标准。
❌ 选项 D (不道德行为)： 这是典型的“红鲱鱼”选项。即使政府意图良好（防止不道德行为），如果手段违反了宪法第一修正案的严格审查标准，该法律依然无效。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip) 在处理言论自由 (Free Speech) 题目时，请遵循以下两步法：
  1. 第一步：判断限制是基于内容 (Content-Based) 还是内容中立 (Content-Neutral)？
    👉 只要法律条文提到具体的话题（如“关于雇主”、“关于政治”），通常就是基于内容的。
  2. 第二步：
    • 如果是基于内容 -> 选 Strict Scrutiny (通常导致违宪)。
    • 如果是内容中立 -> 选 Intermediate Scrutiny (看是否有替代渠道等)。
本题中，一旦你识别出它是“基于内容”的，选项 A 中提到的 "Narrowly Tailored" 和 "Compelling Interest" 关键词就是最直接的线索。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state statute declares that after five years of continuous service in their positions all state employees, including faculty members at the state university, are entitled to retain their positions during "good behavior." The statute also contains a number of procedural provisions. Any state employee who is dismissed after that five-year period must be given reasons for the dismissal before it takes effect. In addition, such an employee must, upon request, be granted a post-dismissal hearing before an administrative board to seek reinstatement and back pay. The statute precludes any other hearing or opportunity to respond to the charges. That post-dismissal hearing must occur within six months after the dismissal takes effect. The burden of proof at such a hearing is on the state, and the board may uphold the dismissal only if it is supported by a preponderance of the evidence. An employee who is dissatisfied with a decision of the board after a hearing may appeal its decision to the state courts. The provisions of this statute are inseverable.
A teacher who had been employed continuously for seven years as a faculty member at the state university was dismissed. A week before the dismissal took effect, she was informed that she was being dismissed because of a charge that she accepted a bribe from a student in return for raising the student's final grade in her course. At that time, she requested an immediate hearing to contest the propriety of her dismissal.
Three months after her dismissal, she was granted a hearing before the state administrative board. The board upheld her dismissal, finding that the charge against her was supported by a preponderance of the evidence presented at the hearing.
The teacher did not appeal the decision of the state administrative board to the state courts. Instead, she sought a declaratory judgment in federal district court to the effect that the state statute prescribing the procedures for her dismissal violates the United States Constitution.
In this case, how should the federal district court rule?

choices.A: Dismiss the suit, because a claim that a state statute is unconstitutional is not ripe for adjudication by a federal court until all judicial remedies in state courts provided for by state law have been exhausted.
choices.B: Hold that the statute is constitutional, because the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment entitles state employees who have a right to their jobs during good behavior only to a statement of reasons for their dismissal and an opportunity for a post-dismissal hearing.
choices.C: Hold that the statute is unconstitutional, because a state may not ordinarily deprive an employee of a property interest in a job without giving the employee an opportunity for some kind of a pre-dismissal hearing to respond to the charges against that employee.
choices.D: Hold that the statute is unconstitutional, because the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment requires a state to demonstrate beyond a reasonable doubt the facts constituting good cause for termination of a state employee.

questions.explanation:
Deprivation of public employment
Type Due process requirements
Termination
(serious) 		• Notice of alleged misconduct
• Pre-termination opportunity to respond to allegation
• Post-termination evidentiary hearing
Suspension without pay
(less serious) 		• Notice of alleged misconduct
• Prompt post-suspension evidentiary hearing

When a state attempts to deprive an individual of life, liberty, or property, the Fourteenth Amendment requires that the state provide procedural due process. To determine the process due, courts balance the government's interest against the individual's interest. And since a public employee who can only be terminated for cause has a property interest in such employment—and termination is a serious deprivation of that interest—due process requires that the employee receive:

  • notice of his/her alleged misconduct
  • a pre-termination opportunity to respond to that allegation and
  • a post-termination evidentiary hearing to determine if the termination was warranted.

Here, the state-university teacher had a property interest in her job because she was entitled to retain her position during "good behavior" and could only be terminated for cause. The university provided the teacher with notice and a post-termination evidentiary hearing. But since the statute precludes any other hearing or opportunity to respond to the charge, she did not have a pre-termination opportunity to respond. Therefore, the court should hold that the statute violates due process (Choice C).

(Choice A) Under the doctrine of administrative remedies, a constitutional claim is not ripe for adjudication until the plaintiff has exhausted all administrative remedies provided by law. But this doctrine does not require plaintiffs to exhaust all state judicial remedies before proceeding to federal court.

(Choice D) Due process does not require a state to prove good cause for terminating an employee. And even if a state chooses to require good cause, due process does not require the state to prove it beyond a reasonable doubt.

📌 Educational Objective

When a public employee can only be fired for cause, procedural due process generally requires that the employee receive (1) notice of any alleged misconduct, (2) a pre-termination hearing to respond to the allegation, and (3) a post-termination evidentiary hearing to determine if the dismissal was warranted.

📚 References
  • Cleveland Bd. of Educ. v. Loudermill, 470 U.S. 532, 542–46 (1985) (explaining the process due when the government terminates a public employee who can only be fired for cause).
questions.zh-question:
某州一项成文法规定，所有州政府雇员，包括州立大学的教职员工，在连续服务满五年后，有权在“行为良好”期间保留其职位。该成文法还包含多项程序性规定。任何在该五年期限后被解雇的州政府雇员，必须在解雇生效前被告知解雇理由。此外，该雇员经请求，必须获得一次解雇后听证，该听证在行政委员会席前举行，以寻求复职和补发薪资。该成文法排除了任何其他听证或回应指控的机会。该解雇后听证必须在解雇生效后六个月内举行。在此类听证中，证明责任由州政府承担，委员会只有在有证据优势支持的情况下才能维持解雇决定。对委员会听证后决定不满的雇员可以向州法院上诉。该成文法的各项规定是不可分割的。

一名在州立大学连续任教七年的教师被解雇。在解雇生效前一周，她被告知，解雇的原因是一项指控，称她收受一名学生的贿赂，以换取提高该学生在她课程中的最终成绩。当时，她请求立即举行听证，以对她被解雇的适当性提出异议。

在她被解雇三个月后，她获得了在州行政委员会席前举行的听证。委员会维持了对她的解雇决定，认定对她的指控有听证会上出示的证据优势支持。

该教师未就州行政委员会的决定向州法院提起上诉。相反，她在联邦地区法院寻求一项宣告性判决，主张规定其解雇程序的州成文法违反了 United States Constitution。

在本案中，联邦地区法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 驳回诉讼，因为在州法律规定的所有州法院司法救济被用尽之前，主张州成文法违宪的诉求尚未成熟，联邦法院不可进行裁决。
zh-choices.B: 裁定该成文法合宪，因为 Fourteenth Amendment 的正当程序条款仅赋予在行为良好期间享有工作权的州政府雇员获得一份解雇理由声明和一次解雇后听证的机会。
zh-choices.C: 裁定该成文法违宪，因为州政府通常不得在未给予雇员某种形式的解雇前听证以回应针对该雇员的指控的机会之前，剥夺雇员在工作中的财产利益。
zh-choices.D: 裁定该成文法违宪，因为 Fourteenth Amendment 的正当程序条款要求州政府必须排除合理怀疑地证明构成终止州政府雇员雇佣关系正当理由的事实。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

Constitutional Law: Procedural Due Process
正确答案 选项 C

裁定该成文法违宪，因为剥夺公共雇员的财产利益（工作）前，必须给予回应指控的机会。

核心考点：程序性正当程序

本题考查的是第十四修正案（14th Amendment）下的程序性正当程序（Procedural Due Process）。解题逻辑分为两步：

第一步：是否存在受保护的利益？

是的。该教师是终身制（tenured）员工，法律规定只能因"行为良好"（即只能因正当理由 for cause）被解雇。这在宪法上构成了对工作的财产利益（Property Interest）。

第二步：剥夺该利益需要什么程序？

当政府剥夺受保护的财产利益时，必须提供正当程序。最高法院在 Cleveland Bd. of Educ. v. Loudermill 案中确立了最低标准。

⚖️ 关键判例规则 (Loudermill Rights) 对于拥有财产利益的公共雇员，在解雇（Termination）之前，必须至少提供：
  • 通知 (Notice)： 告知被指控的不当行为。
  • 解雇前回应机会 (Pre-termination Opportunity to Respond)： 雇员必须有机会在解雇生效前解释自己的立场（"Notice and a hearing"）。
  • 解雇后听证 (Post-termination Hearing)： 全面的证据听证会。
案情应用

本案中的州成文法（Statute）存在致命缺陷：

  • 虽然提供了通知（Notice）。
  • 虽然提供了全面的解雇后听证（Post-termination hearing）。
  • 明确禁止了解雇前的听证或回应机会（"precludes any other hearing or opportunity to respond"）。

由于该法律剥夺了雇员在解雇生效前进行解释或反驳的权利，它直接违反了正当程序条款。因此，联邦法院应裁定该法律违宪。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (Exhaustion of Remedies)
错误。虽然通常需要用尽行政救济，但在提起 §1983 民权诉讼主张违宪时，原告通常不需要先用尽所有的州司法救济（State Judicial Remedies）。此外，本案挑战的是法律本身的合宪性。
选项 B (Post-dismissal only)
错误。仅有解雇后听证是不够的。Loudermill 案明确要求必须有某种形式的“解雇前”程序，哪怕只是简短的口头回应。
选项 D (Beyond a Reasonable Doubt)
错误。这是刑法的证明标准（排除合理怀疑）。在民事雇佣纠纷中，正当程序并不要求如此高的证明标准，通常“优势证据”（Preponderance of the Evidence）即已足够。
💡 MBE 拿分技巧 看到“政府雇员被解雇”的题目，立即检查：
1. 是否是 At-will（随意雇佣）？如果是，通常没有听证权。
2. 是否是 For-cause（因故解雇/终身制）？如果是，必须有 Pre-termination hearing（解雇前听证）。
题目中如果出现“Statute precludes pre-termination hearing”（法律禁止解雇前听证），该法律几乎100%违宪。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state enacted a statute that prohibited children born outside of marriage from receiving welfare benefits that the state provides to children who live in households below the federal poverty line. The purpose of the statute was to encourage individuals to get married before having children.
A man and his unmarried partner had a daughter out of wedlock. Before the man and his partner married, the partner died. The man's annual household income was below the federal poverty line, so he applied for welfare benefits on the daughter's behalf. The state agency overseeing the program denied the application based on the state statute.
The man filed suit in a federal district court, alleging that the state statute violates the equal protection clause.
Which of the following best states the burden of persuasion in the suit?

choices.A: The agency must demonstrate that the state statute is substantially related to an important state interest.
choices.B: The agency must demonstrate that the state statute is the least restrictive means to achieve a compelling state interest.
choices.C: The man must demonstrate that the state statute is not substantially related to an important state interest.
choices.D: The man must demonstrate that the state statute is not the least restrictive means to achieve a compelling state interest.

questions.explanation:
Levels of scrutiny under equal protection clause
Severity of burden
Type of scrutiny
Rational basis
  • no rational
  • relation to
  • legitimate
  • state interest
Intermediate
  • substantial
  • relation to
  • important
  • state interest
Strict
  • necessary to
  • achieve
  • compelling
  • state interest
= challenger's burden = state's burden

A state law that discriminates against similarly situated persons can be challenged under the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. The standard under which a court will review this challenge depends on the alleged discrimination. A law that discriminates against a quasi-suspect class (eg, nonmarital birth) must satisfy intermediate scrutiny. This imposes a difficult burden on the state to prove that the law is substantially related to an important state interest.

Here, a state statute prohibits children born outside of marriage from receiving welfare benefits that the state provides to children who live in households below the federal poverty line. Since this statute discriminates against nonmarital children, the state agency overseeing the welfare program (not the man) has the burden to satisfy intermediate scrutiny (Choice C). Therefore, the agency must demonstrate that the state statute is substantially related to an important state interest.

(Choices B & D) Strict scrutiny applies when a state law discriminates against a suspect class or substantially impacts a fundamental right. This highest level of scrutiny places the burden on the state (not the challenger) to prove that the law is the least restrictive means to achieve a compelling state interest. But since the state statute here discriminates against a quasi-suspect class, intermediate scrutiny applies.

📌 Educational Objective

A state law that discriminates against a quasi-suspect class (eg, nonmarital birth) must satisfy intermediate scrutiny, which imposes the burden on the state to prove that the law is substantially related to an important state interest

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (equal protection clause).
  • Clark v. Jeter, 486 U.S. 456, 461 (1988) (holding that a law discriminating against nonmarital children is subject to intermediate scrutiny).
questions.zh-question:
一个州颁布了一项法规，禁止婚外子女获得该州向生活在联邦贫困线以下家庭的儿童提供的福利金。该法规的目的是鼓励个人在生育子女前结婚。
一名男子和他的未婚伴侣育有一名婚外女儿。在该男子和他的伴侣结婚前，该伴侣去世了。该男子家庭年收入低于联邦贫困线，因此他代表女儿申请福利金。负责该项目的州机构依据该州法规拒绝了该申请。
该男子向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，声称该州法规违反了平等保护条款（equal protection clause）。
以下哪项最能说明该诉讼中的说服责任（burden of persuasion）？

zh-choices.A: 该机构必须证明该州法规与一项重要的州利益（important state interest）有实质性关联（substantially related）。
zh-choices.B: 该机构必须证明该州法规是实现一项紧迫的州利益（compelling state interest）的限制最少的手段（least restrictive means）。
zh-choices.C: 该男子必须证明该州法规与一项重要的州利益没有实质性关联。
zh-choices.D: 该男子必须证明该州法规不是实现一项紧迫的州利益的限制最少的手段。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A police officer was employed on a city's police force for 10 years. When the officer accepted the job, the city's employee benefit plan provided a death benefit to the spouse of any employee who died as a result of any job-related injury. Last year, the city amended its employee benefit plan to deny its death benefit in cases where the death "was caused by the employee's refusal to accept, for any reason, reasonably available medical care prescribed by a physician."
After this amendment took effect, the officer was shot while on duty. Because of a sincerely held religious belief, the officer refused to allow a prescribed blood transfusion and, as a result, died from loss of blood. When the officer's spouse applied for the death benefit, the city denied the application on the basis of the amendment to the employee benefit plan.
The officer's spouse has challenged the amendment, claiming that, as applied to the officer, it violated the officer's constitutional right to the free exercise of religion.
Is the court likely to find the amendment to the employee benefit plan constitutional as applied to the officer?

choices.A: No, because it effectively discriminates against a religious practice.
choices.B: No, because it violates the vested contractual rights of city employees who were hired before the amendment took effect.
choices.C: Yes, because it is generally applicable and religiously neutral, as well as a reasonable limitation on the award of such benefits.
choices.D: Yes, because it imposes a condition only on the award of a government benefit and does not impose a penalty on an individual's conduct.

questions.explanation:
Free exercise analysis
Government burdens
religious belief or conduct
Direct burden
Strict scrutiny
  • burden necessary to achieve
  • compelling state interest

Burden usually
unconstitutional

Incidental burden
Rational basis
  • burden rationally related to
  • legitimate state interest

Burden usually
constitutional

The First Amendment free exercise clause prohibits governments from denying benefits (or imposing burdens) based on an individual's religious belief or conduct (Choice D). The level of scrutiny applied to laws or policies that burden religion depends on whether that burden was:

  • direct (intentional) – triggering strict scrutiny, which invalidates a law unless the government proves that it is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest or
  • incidental (generally applicable and religiously neutral) – triggering rational basis scrutiny, which upholds a law unless the challenger proves that the law has no rational relation to any legitimate government interest.

But even an incidental burden will trigger strict scrutiny when the law requires an individualized assessment of a person's actions.

Here, the employee benefit plan only imposes an incidental burden since the plan is generally applicable to all employees and does not intentionally target religion (ie, is religiously neutral). That is because the plan denies benefits when the refusal to accept medical care was for any reason—it does not single out religious reasons (ie, no individualized assessment). And since the plan is reasonably related to the city's legitimate interest in limiting the award of benefits to job-related deaths, it is likely constitutional.

(Choice A) Although the benefit plan effectively discriminates against the officer's religious practice, the plan will likely be upheld since it is generally applicable and there is no evidence that it intentionally interfered with his religion.

(Choice B) The contracts clause prohibits state and municipal legislatures from enacting laws that substantially impair vested contract rights. But it does not apply to amendments to employee benefit plans since they are unrelated to lawmaking or rulemaking.

📌 Educational Objective

Direct burdens on religion are strictly scrutinized and struck down unless the government proves that the law is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest. In contrast, incidental burdens are upheld unless the challenger proves that the law has no rational relation to any legitimate government interest.

📚 References
  • Emp't Div. v. Smith, 494 U.S. 872, 884–85 (1990) (affirming the government's ability to enforce a generally applicable law that incidentally burdens religion).
questions.zh-question:
一名警官在一个城市的警察部队中受雇了10年。当该警官接受这份工作时，该市的员工福利计划规定，任何因公受伤而死亡的员工的配偶将获得死亡抚恤金。去年，该市修改了其员工福利计划，规定在死亡“因员工出于任何原因拒绝接受医生开具的合理可行的医疗护理”而导致的情况下，拒绝发放死亡抚恤金。

在该修正案生效后，这名警官在执勤时中枪。由于真诚的宗教信仰，该警官拒绝接受医生开具的输血治疗，并因此失血过多而死亡。当该警官的配偶申请死亡抚恤金时，该市根据员工福利计划的修正案拒绝了其申请。

该警官的配偶对该修正案提出质疑，声称该修正案在适用于该警官时，侵犯了其自由行使宗教的宪法权利。

法院是否可能认定该员工福利计划修正案在适用于该警官时符合宪法？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为它实际上歧视了一种宗教实践。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为它侵犯了在该修正案生效前受雇的城市员工的既得合同权利。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为它是普遍适用和宗教中立的，并且是对授予此类福利的合理限制。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为它仅对授予政府福利设定了条件，并未对个人行为施加惩罚。

questions.zh-explanation:
宪法 (Constitutional Law)

MBE 考点解析：自由行使条款

C

正确答案

核心法律规则 (The Rule)

根据美国最高法院在 Employment Division v. Smith (1990) 一案中的裁决：

如果一项法律是普遍适用的 (Generally Applicable) 且 宗教中立的 (Religiously Neutral)，即使它附带地 (Incidentally) 限制了某种宗教行为，也不需要通过严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。

此类法律只需通过合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review)，即只要法律与政府的合法利益有合理关联即可。

本题解析 (Analysis)

要判断法院是否会支持该修正案，我们需要分析该法律的性质：

  • 中立性 (Neutrality)： 该修正案规定拒绝福利的情况是员工“出于任何原因 (for any reason)”拒绝医疗护理。它并没有专门针对宗教原因，也没有将世俗原因排除在外。
  • 普遍适用性 (General Applicability)： 该规定适用于所有城市员工，不针对特定群体。

因此，尽管该规定实际上导致了这位因宗教信仰拒绝输血的警官无法获得福利（附带负担），但因为法律本身是中立和普遍适用的，法院不会应用严格审查。

结论： 政府为了节省开支或限制福利仅用于不可避免的死亡，具有合法利益 (Legitimate Interest)，而该修正案与此利益合理相关。因此，该修正案符合宪法。

⚠️ 高频陷阱：选项 B (合同条款)

很多考生会误选 选项 B，因为该市确实改变了员工入职时的福利条款，这看起来像是违反了合同条款 (Contracts Clause)。

为什么 B 是错的？

请仔细阅读题目的提问 (Call of the Question)：

"...claiming that... it violated the officer's constitutional right to the free exercise of religion."

题目明确问的是基于自由行使宗教权利的挑战是否会成功，而不是基于合同权利的挑战。虽然基于合同条款的挑战可能会成功，但这与本题的诉讼请求（宗教自由）无关。

MBE 技巧： 永远针对题目中特定的法律主张进行回答，不要因为发现了一个潜在的（但未被提出的）违法点而偏离主题。

其他选项排除
  • 选项 A： 错误。虽然法律产生了歧视性的效果，但只要没有歧视性的目的（即法律是中立的），就不会违反自由行使条款。
  • 选项 D： 错误。这涉及“违宪条件原则” (Unconstitutional Conditions)，通常用于政府不能强迫个人放弃权利以换取福利。但在 Smith 案原则下，只要条件是中立通用的，政府通常可以设定福利资格标准。选项 C 的理由更直接切中 Smith 案的要害。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A generally applicable state statute requires an autopsy by the county coroner in all cases of death that are not obviously of natural causes. The purpose of this law is to ensure the discovery and prosecution of all illegal activity resulting in death. In the 50 years since its enactment, the statute has been consistently enforced.
A married couple are sincere practicing members of a religion that maintains it is essential for a deceased person's body to be buried promptly and without any invasive procedures, including an autopsy. When the couple's son died of mysterious causes and an autopsy was scheduled, they filed an action in state court challenging the constitutionality of the state statute and seeking an injunction prohibiting the county coroner from performing an autopsy on their son's body. In this action, the couple claimed only that applying this statute in the circumstances of their son's death would violate their right to the free exercise of religion as guaranteed by the First and Fourteenth Amendments. Assume that no federal statutes are applicable.
Is the state's autopsy statute constitutional as applied to the couple?

choices.A: No, because it is not necessary to vindicate a compelling state interest.
choices.B: No, because it is not substantially related to an important state interest.
choices.C: Yes, because a dead individual is not a person protected by the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.D: Yes, because it is a generally applicable statute and is rationally related to a legitimate state purpose.

questions.explanation:
Free exercise analysis
Government burdens
religious belief or conduct
Direct burden
Strict scrutiny
  • burden necessary to achieve
  • compelling state interest
Incidental burden
Rational basis
  • burden rationally related to
  • legitimate state interest
Burden usually
unconstitutional
Burden usually
constitutional

The First Amendment, applicable to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause, protects an individual's right to freely exercise his/her sincerely held religious beliefs. Any government infringement on this right must satisfy the appropriate level of scrutiny, which depends on the type of burden imposed:

  • direct (intentionally targets religion) – the burden is presumptively invalid and the state must prove that the burden is necessary to achieve a compelling state interest (ie, strict scrutiny)
  • incidental (generally applies to all) – the burden is presumptively valid and the challenger must prove that the burden is not rationally related to any legitimate state interest (ie, rational basis scrutiny)

Here, the couple's sincere religious belief that bodies must be buried promptly and without any invasive procedures was burdened when the county coroner scheduled an autopsy of their son's body. But since a generally applicable state statute requires autopsies for all mysterious deaths like his, that burden is merely incidental. And since autopsies for suspicious deaths are rationally related to a legitimate state purpose—discovering and prosecuting illegal activity resulting in death—the statute is constitutional as applied to the couple.

(Choice A) Had the state intentionally targeted the couple's religion, the state would have needed to prove that the statute was necessary to vindicate a compelling state interest (ie, strict scrutiny).

(Choice B) Under the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause, laws that impact a quasi-suspect class must be substantially related to an important state interest (ie, intermediate scrutiny). But religion is not a quasi-suspect class, so this standard does not apply.

(Choice C) A dead individual is not protected by the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause. But the couple's challenge of the statute is based on their own constitutional rights—not those of their dead son.

📌 Educational Objective

The First Amendment protects the right to freely exercise one's sincerely held religious beliefs. Direct burdens (which target religion) are almost always unconstitutional under strict scrutiny. But incidental burdens (which apply to all) are usually constitutional under rational basis scrutiny.

📚 References
  • Emp't Div. v. Smith, 494 U.S. 872, 885 (1990) (holding that a generally applicable regulation on conduct need not satisfy strict scrutiny to comply with the First Amendment free exercise clause).
questions.zh-question:
一项普遍适用的州法规要求，在所有非明显自然原因导致的死亡案件中，县验尸官必须进行尸检。该法律的宗旨是确保发现并起诉所有导致死亡的非法活动。自该法规颁布以来的50年里，它一直得到持续执行。

一对夫妇是某一宗教的虔诚教徒，该宗教坚称，逝者的遗体必须迅速下葬，且不得经过任何侵入性程序，包括尸检。当这对夫妇的儿子因不明原因死亡，且官方已安排进行尸检时，他们在州法院提起诉讼，质疑该州法规的合宪性，并寻求获得一项禁令，以禁止县验尸官对其子的遗体进行尸检。在该诉讼中，这对夫妇仅主张，在其子死亡的情况下适用该法规，将侵犯他们受 First and Fourteenth Amendments 保障的自由行使宗教信仰的权利。假定没有适用的联邦法规。

该州的尸检法规适用于这对夫妇时是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为它并非为维护一项紧迫的州利益所必需。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为它与一项重要的州利益没有实质性关联。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为逝者并非受 Fourteenth Amendment 正当程序条款保护的“人”。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为它是一项普遍适用的法规，且与一项合法的州目的具有理性关联。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析：自由行使条款

正确答案：D 合宪，因为它是一项普遍适用的法规，且与一项合法的州目的具有理性关联。
核心考点：Smith 规则

根据美国最高法院在 Employment Division v. Smith (1990) 一案中的裁决：

如果一项法律是中立的（Neutral）且普遍适用的（Generally Applicable），即使它附带地（Incidentally）加重了宗教行为的负担，也不违反第一修正案的自由行使条款（Free Exercise Clause）。

此类法律只需通过合理依据审查（Rational Basis Review）。

📝 法律推理分析

本题考察的是当“普遍适用的州法律”与“个人宗教信仰”发生冲突时的审查标准。

  1. 法律性质判断：
    题目明确指出该尸检法规是“普遍适用的”（generally applicable），且目的是为了发现非法活动，并非针对特定宗教（not targeting religion）。
  2. 审查标准选择：
    在 Smith 案之后，对于非针对宗教的普遍性法律，不再适用严格审查（Strict Scrutiny）。只要法律不是为了压制宗教，政府就不需要证明有“紧迫的州利益”（Compelling State Interest）。
  3. 应用合理依据审查：
    法律只需与“合法的州目的”（Legitimate State Purpose）有“理性关联”（Rationally Related）。
    👉 本案中： 调查死因、起诉犯罪是合法的州目的，尸检是实现该目的的理性手段。因此，法律合宪。
❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A (Strict Scrutiny)： 错误。严格审查仅在法律专门针对宗教，或涉及联邦法律（受 RFRA 限制）时才适用。本题是州法律且普遍适用。
选项 B (Intermediate Scrutiny)： 错误。中度审查（实质性关联 + 重要利益）通常用于性别歧视或商业言论等，不适用于自由行使宗教条款的分析。
选项 C (Due Process/Standing)： 错误。虽然死者没有正当程序权利，但本案的原告是父母，他们主张的是自己的宗教自由权利（处理亲属遗体），这足以构成诉讼资格（Standing）。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

看到 Free Exercise Clause（自由行使条款）的题目时，首先判断：

  • 是针对宗教的法律？ ➡️ 选 Strict Scrutiny（通常违宪）。
  • 是普遍适用的中立法律？ ➡️ 选 Rational Basis（通常合宪）。

注意陷阱：如果题目提到 RFRA（宗教自由恢复法案），则联邦行为必须满足严格审查。但本题明确说“无联邦法规适用”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state criminal law prohibits the publication of any description of the details of the execution of any prisoner who is sentenced to death by the courts of the state. Although the law allows a specified number of reporters to observe an execution, only the prison warden's official statement that the prisoner was "executed as provided by law" at a certain time and date may be published. The purpose of the law is to protect the public, particularly children, from the details of executions.
After a particular execution was mishandled, causing the prisoner to suffer, a newspaper in the state published a story describing the event in detail. The story was written by the newspaper's reporter, who was permitted to observe the execution but did not promise prison officials that he would report only the warden's official statement. A prosecutor subsequently filed charges against the newspaper for publishing the details of the execution in violation of the state law.
Is this prosecution constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the prosecution seeks to punish the publication of lawfully obtained, truthful information about a matter of public significance, without adequate justification.
choices.B: No, because the reporter did not promise prison officials that he would report only the warden's official statement about the execution.
choices.C: Yes, because publication of the details of such events might cause psychological damage to some children.
choices.D: Yes, because the newspaper should have brought an action to test the validity of the law before publishing the reporter's story.

questions.explanation:
First Amendment freedoms
Expression Right to communicate information & ideas through speech or conduct
Association Right to form or participate in any group or organization
Press Right to publish truthful information
Religion Free exercise – right to practice religion or no religion without government interference
Establishment – prohibits government from favoring particular religion or religion generally

The First Amendment freedom of the press prohibits the government from unduly restricting the right to publish lawfully obtained and truthful information about matters of public significance. Any government actions that abridge this right must satisfy strict scrutiny, which requires the government to prove that its actions were narrowly tailored (ie, the least restrictive means) to achieve a compelling government interest.

Here, the state prosecuted a newspaper for publishing the truthful details of a mishandled execution that its reporter was permitted to observe. The state may have a compelling interest in protecting the public, particularly children, from the details of executions. But this interest could be achieved by less restrictive means—eg, by requiring a graphic-content warning (Choice C). And since the prosecution lacks adequate justification to survive strict scrutiny, it is unconstitutional.

(Choice B) The prosecution would still be unconstitutional had the reporter promised prison officials that he would report only the warden's official statement about the execution. That is because the published information about the execution was lawfully obtained, truthful, and significant to the public.

(Choice D) The newspaper did not need to bring an action to test the validity of the law before publishing the reporter's story. Instead, it can challenge the law's validity in its defense against this prosecution.

📌 Educational Objective

The First Amendment freedom of the press protects the right to publish lawfully obtained and truthful information about matters of public significance. If the government seeks to abridge this right, it must satisfy strict scrutiny—ie, prove that its actions are narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest.

📚 References
  • Smith v. Daily Mail Pub. Co., 443 U.S. 97, 103 (1979) (holding that the government must satisfy strict scrutiny to justifiably punish the publication of lawfully obtained, truthful information about a matter of public significance).
questions.zh-question:
某州刑事法律禁止公布由该州法院判处死刑的任何囚犯的行刑细节。尽管该法律允许指定数量的记者观察行刑过程，但只允许公布监狱长关于囚犯在特定时间和日期“依法执行死刑”的官方声明。该法律的目的是保护公众，特别是儿童，免受行刑细节的影响。

在一次行刑处理不当，导致囚犯遭受痛苦后，该州一家报纸发表了一篇详细描述该事件的报道。该报道由报社记者撰写，他被允许观察行刑过程，但并未向监狱官员承诺只报道监狱长的官方声明。随后，一名检察官以违反州法律为由，对该报社公布行刑细节的行为提起诉讼。

这项起诉合宪吗？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为该起诉旨在惩罚公布合法获取的、关于具有公共意义事宜的真实信息的行为，而没有充分的正当理由。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为记者没有向监狱官员承诺他只会报道监狱长关于行刑的官方声明。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为公布此类事件的细节可能会对一些儿童造成心理伤害。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为报社在发表记者报道前，应先提起诉讼来检验该法律的有效性。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law / First Amendment

⚖️ 核心法律规则

本题考察的是第一修正案出版自由 (Freedom of the Press) 中的一个经典原则：

规则：如果媒体合法获取 (lawfully obtained) 了关于公共利益事项 (matter of public significance) 的真实信息 (truthful information)，政府原则上不能惩罚其发布行为。

除非政府能证明该惩罚满足严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny) 标准，即：

  • 是为了实现迫切的政府利益 (Compelling government interest)；且
  • 手段是精确剪裁 (Narrowly tailored) 的（即限制最小的手段）。

参考判例：Smith v. Daily Mail Pub. Co. (1979)

🔍 案情逻辑推演

为什么选项 A 是正确的？让我们一步步拆解：

1
信息来源是否合法？
是。记者是被允许进入观察行刑的 (permitted to observe)。虽然他没有承诺只发官方通稿，但他获取信息的方式本身不违法。
2
信息是否真实且具公共意义？
是。死刑执行（特别是处理不当的事故）显然是公众关心的重大政府行为。
3
政府的理由是否通过严格审查？
否。政府的理由是“保护公众（特别是儿童）免受细节影响”。虽然保护儿童可能是一个重要利益，但全面禁止发布并非“限制最小的手段”。

Less restrictive means: 政府可以要求添加警告标签，或者依靠父母的监管，而不是直接剥夺公众的知情权。

🚫 避坑指南 (Distractors)

选项 B 错误：
记者是否承诺并不关键。即使没有承诺，只要信息是合法获取的，宪法权利就优先于法规的限制。如果记者通过非法手段（如非法侵入）获取信息，结果可能不同，但本案中他是获准进入的。

选项 C 错误：
这是政府的抗辩理由，但在宪法天平上，避免“心理不适”不足以压倒对政府行为进行监督的出版自由。这无法通过严格审查。

选项 D 错误：
程序性考点：在刑事诉讼中，被告完全可以以“该法律违宪”作为辩护理由 (Defense)，不需要在发布新闻前先去打一场民事官司来确认法律效力。

💡 MBE 实战技巧：
看到政府惩罚发布真实新闻的题目，首先通过Strict Scrutiny的滤镜。通常情况下，除非涉及国家安全（如军队调动信息），政府很难禁止发布合法获取的真实信息。

关键词记忆：Lawfully obtained + Truthful + Public concern = Protected.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Insurance is provided in a state only by private companies. Although the state insurance commissioner inspects insurance companies for solvency, the state does not regulate their rates or policies. An insurance company charges higher rates for burglary insurance to residents of one part of a county in the state than to residents of another section of the same county because of the different crime rates in those areas.
A resident of that county was charged the higher rate by the insurance company because of the location of her residence. She sues the insurance company, alleging that the differential in insurance rates unconstitutionally denies her the equal protection of the laws.
Will the resident's suit succeed?

choices.A: No, because the constitutional guarantee of equal protection of the laws is not applicable to the actions of these insurance companies.
choices.B: No, because there is a rational basis for the differential in insurance rates.
choices.C: Yes, because the higher crime rate in the resident's neighborhood demonstrates that the county police are not giving persons who reside there the equal protection of the laws.
choices.D: Yes, because the insurance rate differential is inherently discriminatory.

questions.explanation:
State-action doctrine
Traditional government
function
  • Private actor performs traditional & exclusive government function
    (eg, running elections)
Significant government
involvement
  • Government & private actor have mutually beneficial relationship (eg, joint activity or venture)
  • Government creates nexus by affirmatively facilitating or authorizing private action (eg, police officer acting under color of law)
  • Government is pervasively intertwined in private entity's management or control

The Constitution (excluding the Thirteenth Amendment) only applies to government actors. But in rare circumstances, a private actor is viewed as a government actor (and subject to the Constitution) under the state-action doctrine. This doctrine applies when:

  • the private actor performs a traditional and exclusive government function or
  • the government is significantly involved in the private actor's activities.

Therefore, the resident can only challenge the private insurance company's discriminatory conduct on equal protection grounds if the state-action doctrine applies.

Here, the company does not perform a traditional and exclusive government function since insurance has historically been provided by private entities. And though the state inspects all insurance companies for solvency, it does not regulate their rates and policies. But even if it did, state regulation (however substantial) does not amount to significant government involvement since this is an ordinary government activity. Therefore, the resident's suit will fail because equal protection guarantees do not apply to the company's actions.

(Choice B) Equal protection challenges undergo rational basis review when the challenged action does not impact a fundamental right or protected class. But since the insurance company's actions cannot be challenged on equal protection grounds, it does not matter whether there is a rational basis for the insurance rate differential.

(Choices C & D) The higher crime rate in the resident's neighborhood may demonstrate that county police are not giving neighborhood residents the equal protection of the laws. And the insurance rate differential is inherently discriminatory. But these facts are irrelevant in this suit against a private insurance company.

📌 Educational Objective

The state-action doctrine applies when (1) a private actor performs a traditional and exclusive government function or (2) the government is significantly involved in the private actor's activities. The private actor is then treated as a government actor and bound by the Constitution.

📚 References
  • Am. Mfrs. Mut. Ins. Co. v. Sullivan, 526 U.S. 40, 52 (1999) (holding that private insurance companies are not government actors unless there is proof of significant government involvement in their activities).
questions.zh-question:
某州的保险业务仅由私营公司提供。尽管州保险专员会对保险公司的偿付能力进行检查，但州政府并不监管其费率或保单。一家保险公司对该州某县部分地区的居民收取的入室犯法罪保险费率高于同一县另一地区的居民，原因是这些地区的犯罪率不同。

该县的一名居民因其住所位置而被该保险公司收取了较高的费率。她起诉该保险公司，声称保险费率的差异违宪地剥夺了她受法律平等保护的权利。

该居民的诉讼会成功吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为宪法关于法律平等保护的保障不适用于这些保险公司的行为。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为保险费率的差异存在理性基础。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该居民社区较高的犯罪率表明，县警察未能给予居住在此的居民法律的平等保护。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为保险费率的差异本质上是歧视性的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考题解析

宪法 (Constitutional Law) - 个人权利
正确答案：选项 A

不会，因为宪法关于法律平等保护的保障不适用于这些保险公司的行为。

核心考点：州行为理论 (State Action Doctrine)

美国宪法第十四修正案的平等保护条款 (Equal Protection Clause) 仅限制政府（州）的行为，而不限制私人行为。

除非存在例外情况，否则私人公司（如本题中的保险公司）的歧视性行为不构成违宪。

解题逻辑推演
1
识别主体：
题目明确指出保险是由“私营公司” (private companies) 提供的。
2
判断是否构成“州行为”：
私营主体要被视为政府行为者，必须满足以下极其严格的条件之一：
  • 公共职能 (Public Function)： 该实体履行了传统上由政府独占的职能（如选举）。保险显然不是。
  • 纠缠/关联 (Entanglement/Nexus)： 政府必须积极授权、鼓励或促进该违宪行为。
3
分析政府监管：
题目中提到州政府“检查偿付能力” (inspects for solvency) 但“不监管费率” (does not regulate rates)。
单纯的政府监管或发放牌照并不足以将私人行为转化为州行为。
4
结论：
由于没有“州行为”，宪法不适用。无论费率差异多么不公平，原告无法依据宪法起诉。
为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 B (Rational Basis)： 只有确定宪法适用后，才进行审查标准（如理性基础审查）的分析。既然宪法不适用，审查标准就无从谈起。
  • 选项 C & D： 这些选项讨论了事实上的不公平或歧视性。虽然这些可能是事实，但在缺乏“州行为”的前提下，它们不能作为宪法诉讼的依据。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

当你在宪法题中看到被告是私人个体或公司时，第一反应必须是检查是否存在州行为 (State Action)。

如果政府仅仅是颁发执照、提供水电服务或进行一般性监管，通常不构成州行为。如果不存在州行为，直接选择“宪法不适用”类的选项。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A defendant was on trial for a highly publicized capital murder in a federal district court. The court issued an order that prohibited public attendance during voir dire to protect the prospective jurors' privacy, especially concerning sensitive issues. The court issued findings on the record and concluded that public attendance during voir dire would prevent the prospective jurors from answering sensitive questions without suffering personal embarrassment.
Several television networks that are televising the trial have challenged the order, arguing that it is unconstitutional.
Is the court's order likely constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the First Amendment guarantees the press and the public the right to attend criminal trials.
choices.B: No, because there are less restrictive means to protect the privacy of the prospective jurors.
choices.C: Yes, because the court has an interest in protecting prospective jurors from personal embarrassment.
choices.D: Yes, because the court-issued findings on the record warranted closing the proceedings to the public.

questions.explanation:
Right to open courtroom
Public
Press
Criminal defendant
Judge

The First Amendment generally guarantees the press and the public the right to attend every stage of a criminal trial, including voir dire.* However, this right is not absolute, and a court can order that trial proceedings be closed if the court's findings on the record demonstrate that the closure satisfies strict scrutiny ((Choice A)). This requires the court to show that the closure is the least restrictive means to serve a compelling government interest.

Here, the court prohibited the public from attending voir dire in the defendant's murder trial to protect the prospective jurors from personal embarrassment. This promotes the compelling interests of encouraging the prospective jurors to speak frankly about sensitive issues and protecting their privacy—but less restrictive means were available to serve these interests (Choice C). For example, the court could have allowed prospective jurors to answer any sensitive questions outside the presence of the public. Therefore, the order is likely unconstitutional.

*The Supreme Court has not conclusively ruled whether the First Amendment guarantees the press and the public the right to attend civil trials.

(Choice D) The court-issued findings on the record did not warrant closing the proceedings to the public because these findings did not demonstrate that the closure was the least restrictive means to protect the prospective jurors' privacy.

📌 Educational Objective

The First Amendment generally guarantees the press and the public the right to attend criminal trials. However, criminal trial proceedings may be closed when the court demonstrates that the closure satisfies strict scrutiny—ie, that it is the least restrictive means to serve a compelling government interest.

📚 References
  • Press-Enter. Co. v. Super. Ct. of Cal., 464 U.S. 501, 511 (1984) (holding that closing all voir dire proceedings in a criminal trial to the public and press is unconstitutional).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因一起备受瞩目的死刑谋杀案在联邦地区法院受审。法院发布了一项命令，禁止公众在预选陪审员（voir dire）期间旁听，以保护准陪审员的隐私，特别是关于敏感问题的隐私。法院在庭审记录中给出了调查结论，并断定在预选陪审员期间允许公众旁听将使准陪审员因个人尴尬而无法回答敏感问题。

几家正在电视转播该审判的电视网络对该命令提出质疑，认为其违宪。

法院的命令是否可能合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为 First Amendment 保证了媒体和公众有权旁听刑事审判。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为有侵害性更小的方式来保护准陪审员的隐私。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为法院在保护准陪审员免受个人尴尬方面拥有利益。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为法院在庭审记录中给出的调查结论证明了对公众关闭庭审程序的正当性。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Public Access to Trials

⚖️ 核心法律规则 (The Rule) 根据 First Amendment，媒体和公众拥有旁听刑事审判（包括陪审员预选程序 Voir Dire）的推定权利。

这项权利不是绝对的，但关闭庭审必须满足严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny) 标准：
  • 必须为了服务于迫切的政府利益 (Compelling Interest)；
  • 必须有记录在案的调查结论 (Findings on the record) 支持；
  • 措施必须是侵害性最小的手段 (Least Restrictive Means)。
🔍 案情分析

本案中，法官为了保护准陪审员的隐私（避免尴尬），下令完全禁止公众旁听预选陪审员程序。

虽然保护陪审员隐私是一个正当的利益，但法官采取的手段（完全关闭）过于宽泛。法官本可以采取侵害性更小的措施，例如：

  • 仅在询问极度敏感问题时进行非公开询问 (In camera)；
  • 仅对特定的准陪审员进行非公开询问。
✅ 为什么选 B？

选项 B (No, because there are less restrictive means...) 是正确的。

这是宪法第一修正案分析中的关键一环。最高法院在 Press-Enterprise Co. v. Superior Court (1984) 一案中明确指出，如果有关闭庭审的替代方案（即侵害性更小的手段）可以充分保护利益，那么完全关闭庭审就是违宪的。

因为存在“侵害性更小的方式”（如部分非公开询问），所以法院的全面禁令无法通过严格审查。

🚫 陷阱排除
选项 A (First Amendment guarantees...)：
虽然第一修正案确实保障旁听权，但这个选项过于绝对。权利是可以被限制的，只要满足严格审查。选项 B 指出了本案具体的违宪原因（手段不当），比 A 更精准。
选项 C (Interest in protecting jurors...)：
仅仅拥有“利益”是不够的。即使利益是迫切的 (Compelling)，政府采取的手段也必须是必要的且侵害最小的。
选项 D (Findings on the record...)：
虽然法官做了记录，但如果结论本身不支持“这是唯一可行的方法”，或者忽略了替代方案，那么仅仅有记录并不能使违宪的命令变得合宪。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在涉及 First Amendment 限制的问题中，如果政府（法院）限制了言论或旁听权，通常需要进行严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。

看到选项中提到“less restrictive means” (侵害性更小的手段) 或 “narrowly tailored” (狭义剪裁) 时，要高度警惕。这往往是政府行为违宪的致命伤——即手段过重，打击面过广。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.topic: Applicability of Bill of Rights to states
questions.question:
A state statute requires all workers' compensation actions filed in state court to be decided by a judge. A woman brought a workers' compensation action in state court against her employer for injuries she sustained at work. The woman demanded a jury trial, but the court denied her request pursuant to the state statute.
Is the state statute likely constitutional?

choices.A: No, because denying a jury trial only in workers' compensation actions violates equal protection of the laws.
choices.B: No, because the Seventh Amendment guarantees the woman a jury trial.
choices.C: No, because the Sixth Amendment requires a jury to decide the outcome of the case.
choices.D: Yes.

questions.explanation:
Applicability of Bill of Rights to states
Bill of Rights
Congress of the United States
Applicable to states under the 14th
Amendment due process clause
Exceptions
Ban on quartering soldiers
(3rd Amendment)
Right to grand jury Indictment
(5th Amendment)
Right to civil jury trial
(7th Amendment)

The first 10 amendments to the U.S. Constitution (ie, the Bill of Rights) protect individuals from government overreach. These protections limit the power of the federal government, and most apply to the states with equal force through incorporation into the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause—with three exceptions:

  • The Third Amendment prohibition against the government quartering soldiers in individuals' homes
  • The Fifth Amendment requirement of a grand jury indictment to charge a person with a capital offense
  • The Seventh Amendment guarantee of a jury trial in civil cases*

Here, the state court denied the woman's jury trial demand pursuant to a state statute requiring judges to decide the outcome of workers' compensation suits. Since the right to a jury trial in civil cases has not been incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause, this right does not apply in state court. As a result, the woman has no right to a jury trial, and the statute is likely constitutional (Choice B).

*The Supreme Court incorporates a protection under the Bill of Rights into the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause if the protection is fundamental to the scheme of ordered liberty or deeply rooted in the history and tradition of the United States.

(Choice A) The statute implicates the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause because it treats workers' compensation claimants differently than other civil claimants. However, the statute does not substantially impact a fundamental right or protected class, so rational basis scrutiny applies. Since this low level of scrutiny is easily met, the statute likely complies with the equal protection clause.

(Choice B) The Seventh Amendment right to a jury trial in civil cases has not been incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause. Thus, this right does not apply in state court. As a result, the woman has no right to a jury trial.

(Choice C) The Sixth Amendment right to a jury trial attaches to any criminal proceeding in which the defendant could be sentenced to more than six months in prison. But since the woman filed a civil action, this right does not apply here.

📌 Educational Objective

Every Bill of Rights protection applies to the states except (1) the Third Amendment prohibition against the government quartering soldiers in individuals' homes, (2) the Fifth Amendment requirement of a grand jury indictment for capital offenses, and (3) the Seventh Amendment right to a jury trial in civil cases.

📚 References
  • Minneapolis & St. Louis R.R. Co. v. Bombolis, 241 U.S. 211, 217–18 (1916) (explaining that the Seventh Amendment right to a jury trial in civil cases does not apply to the states).
  • McDonald v. City of Chi., 561 U.S. 742, 765 n.13 (2010) (reaffirming that the Seventh Amendment guarantee of a civil jury trial has not been incorporated into the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause).
questions.zh-question:
某州法律规定，所有在州法院提起的工伤赔偿诉讼都必须由法官裁决。一名女性因在工作中受伤，在州法院对其雇主提起了工伤赔偿诉讼。该女性要求进行陪审团审判，但法院根据州法律驳回了她的请求。

该州法律是否可能合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为仅在工伤赔偿诉讼中拒绝陪审团审判违反了法律的平等保护原则。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为Seventh Amendment保障了该女性获得陪审团审判的权利。
zh-choices.C: 否，因为Sixth Amendment要求由陪审团决定案件的结果。
zh-choices.D: 是。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law · Individual Rights
✅
正确答案：选项 D (Yes)
该州法律是合宪的。
核心考点：权利法案的“并入” (Incorporation)

本题考察的是权利法案 (Bill of Rights) 中的条款是否适用于州政府。

虽然大多数权利法案的保护通过第十四修正案的正当程序条款 (14th Amendment Due Process Clause) 适用于各州（即“并入”），但仍有少数例外。

⚠️ 必须记住的三个例外

以下权利尚未并入第十四修正案，因此不强制州法院遵守：

  • Seventh Amendment (第七修正案)
    民事案件中的陪审团审判权 (Right to jury trial in civil cases)。
  • Fifth Amendment (第五修正案)
    死刑/重罪案件的大陪审团起诉权 (Right to grand jury indictment)。
  • Third Amendment (第三修正案)
    禁止士兵驻扎民宅 (Prohibition against quartering soldiers)。
⚖️ 法律推理

在本案中，原告在州法院 (State Court) 提起的是民事诉讼 (Civil Action)——即工伤赔偿诉讼。

虽然第七修正案 (7th Amendment) 保证在联邦法院的民事案件中享有陪审团审判的权利，但最高法院明确裁定，这一权利并未并入第十四修正案。

因此，各州有权自行决定是否在民事案件（如工伤赔偿）中提供陪审团。既然该州法律规定由法官裁决，该法律并未违反美国宪法。

❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A (Equal Protection): 错误。虽然该法律区别对待工伤赔偿案件和其他民事案件，但这不涉及“基本权利”或“受保护阶层”。法院仅需适用合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review)。为了司法效率而限制陪审团审判是“合理”的，因此不违宪。
选项 B (7th Amendment): 错误。如上所述，第七修正案仅约束联邦法院，不约束州法院。
选项 C (6th Amendment): 错误。第六修正案仅适用于刑事案件 (Criminal Prosecutions)，本案是民事诉讼。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state administrative agency employs individuals on a permanent and seasonal basis. Some seasonal employees are rehired at the end of their work period, but most are not. On rare and random occasions, the agency has given seasonal employees who were not rehired a statement of reasons and an opportunity for a hearing. No statute or agency rule requires a statement of reasons or an opportunity for a hearing.
A man who was hired as a seasonal employee of the agency was not rehired at the end of his work period. The man was not given a statement of reasons or an opportunity for a hearing.
The man sued the agency in federal court, requesting a statement of reasons and a hearing.
Will the man's suit likely succeed?

choices.A: No, because the man has no property interest entitling him to procedural due process.
choices.B: No, because the Tenth Amendment reserves to the states the power to set the conditions of state employment.
choices.C: Yes, because the agency's procedure constituted a bill of attainder.
choices.D: Yes, because the agency's procedure denied the man the equal protection of the laws.

questions.explanation:
Procedural due process
Person intentionally deprived of life,
liberty, or property by:
Federal government
(5th Amendment)

process due
Yes
State or municipality
(14th Amendment)
No
process due

Did government give reasonable
notice of actions against person?

Was there a meaningful
opportunity to be heard by a neutral decision-maker?

Constitutional
No → Unconstitutional
No → Unconstitutional
No → Unconstitutional

The man's claim invokes the Fourteenth Amendment right to procedural due process, which requires states to follow certain procedures when they intentionally deprive a person of life, liberty, or property. These procedures include giving persons:

  • notice of the charges, proceedings, or other actions against them and
  • a meaningful opportunity to be heard by a neutral decision-maker.

Public employees are only entitled to these procedures if they have a property interest in their employment. This exists when the employee (1) has an ongoing employment contract, (2) can only be fired for cause, or (3) receives assurances of continued employment. But since none of these conditions apply to a seasonal (ie, probationary) public employee, the man had no property interest entitling him to due process. Therefore, his suit requesting a statement of reasons and a hearing will likely fail.

(Choice B) Under the Tenth Amendment, all powers not expressly granted to the federal government by the Constitution—including the power to set the conditions of state employment—are reserved to the states. But when exercising such powers, states must comply with other constitutional provisions (eg, procedural due process).

(Choice C) A bill of attainder is a legislative act that punishes a specified person or group without a judicial trial. But since the agency's procedure is applied against random persons, it is not a bill of attainder.

(Choice D) The equal protection clause prohibits the government from treating similarly situated people differently—even unintentionally—without adequate justification. But when, as here, the government does not substantially impact a fundamental right or protected class, its actions will likely be upheld under rational basis scrutiny.

📌 Educational Objective

Public employees have a protected property interest in their jobs if they (1) have an ongoing employment contract, (2) can only be fired for cause, or (3) receive assurances of continued employment. Therefore, seasonal (ie, probationary) public employees can be terminated without due process.

📚 References
  • Bd. of Regents of State Colls. v. Roth, 408 U.S. 564, 576–77 (1972) (explaining when public employees have a protected interest in continued employment).
questions.zh-question:
一个州行政机构雇佣长期和季节性雇员。部分季节性雇员在工作期满后被续聘，但大多数未被续聘。在少数随机情况下，该机构曾向未被续聘的季节性雇员提供理由陈述和举行听证会的机会。没有任何法规或机构规定要求提供理由陈述或举行听证会的机会。

一名被该机构雇佣为季节性雇员的男子，在工作期满后未被续聘。该男子未被给予理由陈述或举行听证会的机会。

该男子在联邦法院起诉该机构，要求提供理由陈述和举行听证会。

该男子的诉讼是否可能成功？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该男子不具有使其有权享有 procedural due process 的财产权益。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为 Tenth Amendment 将设定州政府雇佣条件的权力保留给各州。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该机构的程序构成了一项 bill of attainder。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该机构的程序剥夺了该男子享有 equal protection of the laws 的权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：程序性正当程序 (Procedural Due Process)
✅ 正确答案：选项 A

本题的核心考点在于判断公职人员是否拥有受宪法保护的财产权益 (Property Interest)。

法律依据与推理

第十四修正案 (14th Amendment) 规定，州政府在剥夺任何人的生命、自由或财产之前，必须给予正当程序（通常指通知和听证会）。

分析步骤如下：

  1. 第一步：是否存在被剥夺的“生命、自由或财产”？
  2. 第二步：如果存在，需要什么样的程序？

在本案中，关键在于第一步。对于公职雇佣关系，只有当雇员对该职位拥有“合法的权利主张” (Legitimate Claim of Entitlement) 时，才构成受保护的“财产权益”。

Board of Regents v. Roth (1972)
最高法院裁定：如果公职人员的雇佣是“随意”的 (At-will)，或者是固定期限且没有续约承诺的，那么他在合同期满后没有宪法保护的财产权益，政府无需提供听证会。

结合本题事实：

  • 该男子是季节性雇员 (Seasonal Employee)。
  • 没有法规或规则要求必须续聘。
  • 虽然机构偶尔随机给过其他人听证会，但这并未形成具有约束力的规则或相互理解 (Mutual Understanding)。

因此，该男子对续聘只有单方面的“期望”，而非合法的“权利”。没有财产权益，就没有正当程序权利。

为什么其他选项是错的？
❌ 选项 B (Tenth Amendment)：
虽然第十修正案保留了州的权力，但州在行使权力时必须遵守第十四修正案的正当程序条款。如果存在财产权益，州就不能随意剥夺。
❌ 选项 C (Bill of Attainder)：
褫夺公权法案 (Bill of Attainder) 是指立法机关未经审判直接惩罚特定个人或群体的法案。本案是行政机构的雇佣决定，且不涉及刑事性质的惩罚，故不适用。
❌ 选项 D (Equal Protection)：
虽然机构的行为看起来不一致（随机给听证会），但这不一定违反平等保护条款 (Equal Protection)。除非涉及嫌疑分类（如种族）或基本权利，否则政府行为只需通过合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review)。行政上的不一致通常不足以构成违宪。
💡 MBE 破题技巧 在做涉及解雇公职人员的题目时，寻找以下关键词来判断是否有“财产权益”：
  • 有权益 (Right to Hearing)： "For Cause" (因故解雇)、"Tenure" (终身教职)、"Contract for a term" (未到期的合同)。
  • 无权益 (No Hearing)： "At Will" (随意雇佣)、"Probationary" (试用期)、"Seasonal" (季节性)、"End of Contract" (合同期满不续约)。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A city ordinance created a three-member zoning board, which is responsible for approving the location of all entertainment venues in the city. In an inseverable provision, the ordinance requires that one member of the board be a representative of the local council of churches.
A minister was appointed to the board to represent the local council of churches. During the minister's tenure, the board denied a company permission to open a nightclub in a particular location solely because it would be so close to an existing church that it might disturb the church's operations. The company has challenged the ordinance and its application in federal court on constitutional grounds.
Is the company likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the existing church has a right to have its vested property interests protected.
choices.B: No, because the minister was only one of three votes and, therefore, could not dictate the decision of the zoning board.
choices.C: Yes, because, as applied, the ordinance denied the company the equal protection of the laws by irrationally discriminating against its particular type of business.
choices.D: Yes, because the requirement that the zoning board include a representative of the local council of churches violates the First and Fourteenth Amendments.

questions.explanation:
